name: Question 3
problem:
$$
{\begin{aligned}{x}^{′}(t)=-5x(t)+y(t) \\ {y}^{′}(t)=-4x(t)-y(t)\end{aligned}
$$

Consider the system of linear differential equations above. The eigenvector $v=[1,\text{ }2]^{T}$ corresponds to the repeated eigenvalue $\lambda =-3$ of the system's matrix $A.$ The vector $w=[0,\text{ }1]^{T}$ is such that $(A-\lambda I)w=v.$ Select the correct options in the reasoning below.The general solution of the system is

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}x(t) \\ y(t)\end{aligned}] & ={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]{e}^{-3t}+{c}_{2}([\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]t{e}^{-3t}+[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{{field-1}}) \\  & ={c}_{1}{e}^{-3t}{{field-2}}+{c}_{2}{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}t \\ 2t+1\end{aligned}],\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.\end{aligned}
$$

The line that passes through the origin and is parallel to $v=[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$ has the equation 

$$
y={{field-3}}
$$

and the straight-line solutions of the form
${c}_{1}{e}^{-3t}[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 2\end{aligned}]$
lie on that line. 

Since ${e}^{-3t}\to $ 
{{field-4}} 
as $t\to \infty ,$ these solutions approach 
{{field-5}}  
as $t\to \infty .$
